what_matters.tag_note: Anthropic IPO · priced Wed evening New York · trades tonight
what_matters.head: Anthropic priced its share sale at $83, above the $70 to $78 range, and starts trading on Nasdaq tonight under the ticker ANT.
what_matters.detail: The sale grew to about 980 million shares from the 825 million planned and raises $81.3B, the largest on record (CNBC, citing the company's release). That values Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion. Bloomberg reported the price at about 05:15 SGT Thursday, after the US close (Yahoo Finance's live page). A filing on Wednesday registers 178.25 million more shares, of which 23.25 million are for the underwriters' option. The final prospectus was not on the SEC's site at 13:35 SGT. The seven-company $26B placement is at the IPO price (CNBC). The opening time is not announced.

what_matters.tag_note: Fed minutes · out 03:00 SGT Thu · gold and oil
what_matters.head: Gold fell 3.77% on Wednesday, about 2.7 times its usual daily move, to its lowest in 14 months as the Fed's minutes pointed to a rate rise in December.
what_matters.detail: Nearly all Fed officials expect a quarter-point rise in December, and two raised the possibility of a half point (AP). Governor Waller said he is very concerned about inflation and that a half point might be needed (Investopedia). Before the minutes, futures put the chance of a quarter point at 92% and a half point at 8% (CME FedWatch, per CNBC). The dollar reached a 19-month high (Reuters). US crude fell 4.64%, about 1.5 times its usual day; Investopedia put that down to news of rising global supply and gave no detail. The Fed decides on 9 Dec New York time, which is 03:00 SGT on Thu 10 Dec.

what_matters.tag_note: Soitec · results out · Wed 18 Nov after the Paris close
what_matters.head: Soitec's second-quarter revenue rose 50% to €204M, and it says customers have committed about US$1.2B under contracts for its optical-chip wafers.
what_matters.detail: The growth rate is at constant currency and scope. Revenue from AI and data-centre products was €107M, up 109%. Photonics-SOI, the wafers used for optical links in data centres, brought in about US$75M in the quarter. Most Photonics-SOI customers have signed capacity contracts backed by cash deposits; the release gives no count and no names. For the full year Soitec expects revenue up about 40%, Photonics-SOI revenue above US$300M and a gross margin slightly above 30%. Paris trading today, from 16:00 SGT, is the first since the results. Today's report still lists the results as due. Its Soitec price is Wednesday's close, from before the results.

after_data.text: After-hours quotes in the report: Nvidia up 0.66%, Amazon 1.34%, AMD 1.29%, Broadcom 1.58%, Micron 1.86% and CoreWeave 1.88%. These are not in Wednesday's US closing prices.

Taiwan's index fell 3.9% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng 1.9%. South Korea's KOSPI fell 0.5%, with Samsung down 1.59% and SK Hynix down 1.22%. Japan's Nikkei rose 0.3% (Investing.com, later in the session than the 12:05 SGT prices here). AFP's earlier snapshot had the KOSPI down 1.1%. On Singapore the two disagree: Investing.com's text says the Straits Times Index fell 1.03%; AFP says Singapore rose. AFP cites the Nvidia crisis, the Fed minutes and Monday's US rule on remote access to chips. Not in Wednesday's US prices.

The three leaders are due to meet in Shenzhen today, after the morning APEC session. Nuclear arms and the wars in Ukraine and Iran are on the agenda (AP). No outcome was reported when this was written.

out.text: First half (six months to 30 Sep): revenue €317M, up 39% at constant currency and scope. EBITDA €103M, a 32.5% margin against 34.1% a year earlier. Operating income €20M against a €35M loss. Net loss €45M after one-off items. Free cash flow €236M, including €86M of customer deposits for Photonics-SOI. Net cash €169M against net debt of €56M at 31 Mar. The French tax dispute ended with an agreement on 7 Aug: Soitec gives up about €320M of tax-loss carryforwards and expects to pay about €42M in the third quarter. Planned capital spending for the year rises to about €130M from about €100M.

Investing.com's mid-morning note cited new price-target cuts after last week's results: UBS to $155 from $250, Needham to $200 from $300 and Mizuho to $240 from $300. It also cited a law firm's investor alert on 17 Nov, a share sale by the investor Eclipse on 16 Nov, and worry about reliance on big customers. OpenAI was 25% of Cerebras's revenue in the nine months to 30 Sep 2026 (its 10-Q).

Rose 2.7% early on Tuesday night's results, then closed lower, its fifth straight fall (AP, Yahoo Finance). Reuters says the forecast did not clear up the uncertainty after Huang's resignation and puts the shares 36% below their 6 Oct record close.
No reported cause found. The fall came on more than twice the usual volume, two days before its Q3 results.

latest.tape_note: The S&P 500 fund fell 0.31%, the index's fifth straight fall (AP). The Dow lost 1.1%. UnitedHealth fell 10% and Humana 13% on worry about closer regulation of health insurers (Investopedia). The Nasdaq 100 fund rose 0.39% and the chip fund 0.28%; the chip fund is down 8.7% over five sessions. The VIX fell 3.53% and is up 40.4% over five sessions.
